entries.spiritual_meaning: The Infinite Divine Love itself — the Lord's own Esse from which all things proceed
entries.definition: As the originating source of all cosmic being in the natural text, this figure corresponds to the Divine Love that is the origin of all spiritual life. The 'greatness' is the infinity of love; 'established' denotes self-subsistence; dwelling in his own 'light-earth' denotes infinite good as the ground of all being.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too narrow — the Father is not merely good but the infinite origin of both love and wisdom.

entries.notes: Called 'love' itself in the text's own definition. The five 'limbs' of the Father (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) correspond to five discrete faculties of the Divine, mapping to Swedenborg's teaching that the Divine has infinite attributes perceived as distinct by finite minds.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord as Divine Human descending into spiritual combat — the celestial principle of good proceeding from Divine Love
entries.definition: As the first being sent forth from the Father into battle against Darkness, the First Man corresponds to the Lord's own Rational or Celestial Human — the Divine Good made operative, clothed in truths, that descends into the deepest hells to confront and overcome evil. He is the head of all regeneration.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: While the First Man carries divine wisdom, his primary function is as Divine Good proceeding into combat — the celestial will, not merely wisdom.

entries.notes: The five sons of the First Man are the five faculties of spiritual perception. The First Man's descent, combat, wounding, and ascent form the universal archetype of all temptation and regeneration. Corresponds to what Swedenborg calls the Lord's combat against the hells from His Divine Rational.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's Divine Truth proceeding in judicial and creative power — the operative divine that orders, judges, and constructs the spiritual world
entries.definition: As the being who rescues the First Man, constructs the universe, and judges the rulers, the Living Spirit corresponds to Divine Truth proceeding from the Lord's love in its governing, judging, and ordering function. It builds the discrete degrees of the mind and restrains evil within its appointed bounds.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Providence is one aspect; the Living Spirit's primary function is as proceeding truth in its judicial and constructive power.

entries.notes: The Living Spirit performs seven works and constructs five great things. Its five sons correspond to five derivative truths governing the structural order of the spiritual world. Called 'Father of Life' because divine truth in act is the immediate source of all spiritual life in created beings.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Lord's Divine Truth proceeding as mediating influx — the divine manifestation that purifies wisdom from its admixture with falsity
entries.definition: As the figure who displays his image to purify the light, the Third Ambassador corresponds to the third proceeding of the Divine — truth made visible as a mediating presence between celestial and natural degrees. His image, displayed before the powers, draws captive good upward while expelling evil downward.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: While providence is an aspect, the Ambassador's distinctive function is as mediating truth made visible — the displayed divine image — not providence in general.

entries.notes: The Ambassador's image is the pivotal act of the cosmic drama: it simultaneously purifies light and provokes the fall of evil. Ten works result from his advent. The text distinguishes his advent from the First Man's and the Living Spirit's, showing three discrete modes of divine operation.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Truth as generative matrix — the proceeding wisdom that gives birth to all spiritual life
entries.definition: As the being from whom the First Man proceeds and who intercedes for his rescue, the Mother of Life corresponds to the Divine Proceeding as life-giving truth — the formative wisdom from which all derivative goods and truths are born. She is the first emanation from the Father.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: While she proceeds from love, her function is specifically as truth/wisdom in its generative and nurturing aspect — the womb from which spiritual forms are born.

entries.notes: Called the 'first Holy Spirit' — the first proceeding from the Divine. Her 'grief' over captive souls corresponds to the Lord's mercy. She spent an immeasurable duration within the Father before proceeding forth — describing the infinite preparation within Divine Love before truth goes forth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Wisdom in its radiant, illuminating, and saving power — the Lord's truth made manifest for liberation
entries.definition: As the figure who hunts souls, gives hope to Adam, and wages the fourth war, Jesus the Splendour corresponds to divine truth in its fullness of glory proceeding to illuminate, liberate, and redeem the interiors of the human spirit. His twelve wisdoms are the complete truths derived from good.

variant_readings.reading: Divine Truth in its saving power
variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Accurate but incomplete — 'Splendour' specifically denotes the radiant, illuminating quality that distinguishes this proceeding from others.

entries.notes: The fourth 'day' and the fourth 'hunter.' His advent to Adam and Eve represents the descent of divine truth into the natural will and understanding. His ship is the ship of living waters — the vessel of truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pure uncorrupted wisdom — the pristine affection of truth proceeding from celestial good
entries.definition: As the being who captivates the rulers through her beauty and guides the soul at death, the Virgin of Light corresponds to the pure, uncorrupted perception of truth from good — divine wisdom in its pristine, virginal form that has never been contaminated by self-love. She guides regeneration from first to last.
entries.notes: She 'takes away the heart of the rulers' — dispossesses dominant falsities of their power through reflected spiritual beauty. Called 'soul of the father' — the inmost life of Divine Good. Circulates through the whole zone ascending and descending — truth pervading all degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Wisdom entering the understanding — interior illumination that awakens the rational mind from spiritual dormancy
entries.definition: As the being who awakens sleepers, gathers the scattered, and enters the body to humble its guardians, the Light Mind corresponds to the influx of divine intelligence into the human understanding — the specific operation by which the Lord opens the rational mind to perceive truth.
entries.notes: The fourth father and the eleventh judge. When it enters the body, it humbles the guardians (evil affections at the gates of the senses) and opens the orifices to good. Corresponds to what Swedenborg calls illustration — divine light entering the rational mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The sustaining axis of Divine Truth connecting the lowest natural degree to the highest celestial — the fully regenerated Divine Human form
entries.definition: As the column extending from earth to heaven that bears all burdens and through which light ascends, the Pillar of Glory corresponds to the ordered pathway of Divine Truth that sustains and connects all discrete degrees — and to the fully regenerated human as the complete form of that truth.
entries.notes: Called both 'Pillar of Glory' and 'Perfect Man' — truth as structure and truth as living form. Sustains 'all the weights of the universe.' Corresponds to the Word as the connective axis between degrees — the means through which all ascent from natural to celestial proceeds.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The proprium — the corporeal, self-derived will that fashions all appearances of life from what is spiritually dead
entries.definition: As the female power that sculpts the world, fashions Adam and Eve, and gives strength to the King of Darkness, Matter corresponds to the unregenerate proprium — the inherited corporeal will that shapes external forms but has no spiritual life in itself. Called 'thought of death' because it is the origin of all spiritual death.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too narrow — Matter is specifically the formative, corporeal will from which evil takes its shapes, not just desire.

entries.notes: Called 'sculptress' because the proprium gives external form to what is spiritually nothing. Always female in the text — corresponding to the receptive/volitional function. Fashions both the worlds of darkness and the human body — the same proprium that gives rise to hells also provides the corporeal basis for natural life.

natural_variants: King of the realms of Darkness
entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling love of self — the sovereign principle of all evil, governing all the realms of falsity from its seat in the deepest obscurity of self-love
entries.definition: As the five-headed ruler who wages war against the light, the King of Darkness corresponds to the love of self in its fully organized, sovereign form — the single ruling evil from which all other evils and falsities derive. His five shapes represent five genera of evil; his kingdom is the totality of hell.
entries.notes: Has no genuine spiritual life — his 'life' is the reactive agitation of self-love. Can only perceive what is immediately present, not what is remote — evil lacks all genuine foresight. Hardened beyond any truth — impervious to penetration. His five shapes map to five genera of infernal evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The spiritual form in which Divine Truth is received and made visible at the threshold of death — the representative image of the Divine that meets the departing soul
entries.definition: As the being that appears at the moment of death bearing gifts and calming the departing soul, the Light Form corresponds to the form of divine truth accommodated to the individual's reception — the spiritual representative that greets the spirit as it leaves the natural body.
entries.notes: The fifth father. Appears with three angels bearing prize, garment, and crown — corresponding to the good of life, external truths, and wisdom. The 'Light Form' is the personalized manifestation of divine truth for each individual at the threshold between natural and spiritual life.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Wisdom that constructs and organizes the interior structures of the regenerating mind and the new heaven
entries.definition: As the architect who builds the new aeon, the Great Builder corresponds to the ordering intelligence of the Divine that constructs the new heaven and the interior forms of the regenerate mind. He builds both the dwelling for the Divine and the prison for evil.
entries.notes: The fourth judge. Builds both the 'new aeon of joy' and the prison for the enemy — regeneration necessarily includes both the construction of heavenly states and the permanent confinement of evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine Good made manifest through wisdom — the union of love and truth as received and cherished by all heavenly societies
entries.definition: As the honored figure who proceeds from the Father, the Beloved of the Lights corresponds to the Divine Good as it is loved and received by all who are in wisdom — the conjunction of love and truth that the angels perceive and adore.
entries.notes: Associated with the household of the angels. His province encompasses all who receive and transmit divine truth in love. The second emanation from the Father.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine wisdom — truth proceeding from love that illuminates the understanding
entries.opposite_sense: Falsity from evil — the absence of all wisdom and truth
entries.definition: Light is the universal correspondence for wisdom because, as natural light makes objects visible to the eye, divine wisdom makes spiritual realities perceptible to the understanding. Light flows from its source (love) and illuminates all it touches.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Synonymous but less precise — 'wisdom' encompasses the full reception of truth in the understanding, which is how the text consistently uses 'light.'

entries.notes: The single most frequent term in the corpus. The 'light elements' are scattered wisdom held captive in the natural mind. The 'Cross of Light' is the suffering of wisdom bound within the natural order. Light that has 'not tasted death' is pristine wisdom; light that was mixed and purified is restored wisdom.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Falsity from evil — the total absence of divine wisdom and truth
entries.opposite_sense: Wisdom and divine truth
entries.definition: Darkness corresponds to falsity from evil because, as natural darkness renders all things invisible and formless, spiritual darkness — falsity arising from self-love — renders the understanding incapable of perceiving any spiritual reality. It is not a substance but a privation.
entries.notes: The text teaches that darkness is inscrutable even to itself — evil has no self-reflective intelligence. Night does seven evils corresponding inversely to the seven goods done by the sun. The 'land of darkness' is the total state of the unregenerate will.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine love — celestial love in its ardent, consuming, and purifying quality
entries.opposite_sense: Self-love — the consuming fire of the proprium that devours and destroys
entries.definition: Fire corresponds to love because both are the animating, consuming force from which all activity proceeds. Positive fire (living fire) is divine love that warms, purifies, and gives life. Negative fire (dark fire) is self-love that consumes, destroys, and devours all it encounters.
entries.notes: The text carefully distinguishes 'living fire' from 'dark fire.' The living fire is the first and inmost garment of the First Man. It exists in eight places — eight states of the spiritual order. The 'great fire' at the end is divine love in its final purifying judgment. Fire separates four things from wood: love, wisdom, dead residue, and falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Truth in its flowing, purifying, and sustaining quality
entries.opposite_sense: Falsity — corrupted truth that flows pervasively and perverts all it touches
entries.definition: Water corresponds to truth because both flow from a source, find their level, cleanse what they contact, and sustain life. 'Living waters' are truths flowing from divine good; corrupted waters are falsified truths that carry the poison of evil throughout the mind.
entries.notes: The ship of living waters is the vessel of truth. The 'salty inner sea' is sensory falsity corrupted by the residue of washed-out evils. The 'garment of waters' is the external containment of truth given to rulers of death — a key image of how divine truth is administered even to evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual influx — the breath of the Divine flowing into the understanding as the sphere of rational perception
entries.opposite_sense: False persuasion — vain reasoning from the proprium that sweeps through the mind
entries.definition: Wind corresponds to spiritual influx and the rational sphere because, like wind, influx is invisible yet perceptible through its effects. The 'living air' is the atmosphere of genuine spiritual perception proceeding from the Divine. Dark wind is the persuasive force of reasoning from falsity.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: The rational is one function; 'wind' more broadly represents the whole sphere of spiritual influx and perception.

entries.notes: The living air is the one garment that was not wounded in the first combat — the rational sphere of spiritual life remains unpenetrated by falsity. It becomes 'a spirit of life' to the other four elements. Corresponds to the spiritual atmosphere or sphere that Swedenborg describes surrounding every angel.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscurity of understanding arising from self-love — dense falsity that blinds the intellect
entries.definition: Smoke corresponds to the obscurity of understanding because, as natural smoke rises from fire and obscures vision, spiritual smoke rises from the fire of self-love and darkens the intellectual sight. It is the first and most basic product of infernal love.
entries.notes: The world of Smoke is the first and ruling world of darkness — intellectual obscurity from self-love is the head of all other evils. The King of Smoke is the chief ruler. Gold is the body of Smoke's rulers — the external semblance of good covering intellectual blindness. Its taste is salty.

natural_variants: five sons of the First Man
entries.spiritual_meaning: The five essential faculties of spiritual perception — the complete set of divine powers clothing and protecting the celestial will
entries.opposite_sense: Five elements of darkness — five fundamental forms of evil
entries.definition: The five light elements (fire, wind, water, light, air) correspond to five essential faculties of the spiritual mind: celestial love, spiritual influx, truth, wisdom, and rational perception. They clothe the First Man as armor because they are the truths that protect the will in spiritual combat.
entries.notes: The fivefold pattern is the most architecturally significant in the text. Each element carries five sub-powers, yielding twenty-five. Together with the summons and obedience, the system expands. The five dark elements (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) are the inverted counterparts — five genera of evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A state of spiritual life — a heavenly society or discrete degree of the Lord's kingdom
entries.opposite_sense: Worlds of darkness — infernal states
entries.definition: An aeon corresponds to a state of spiritual life because, like a region of existence, it is a bounded sphere of reception determined by the quality of love that animates it. 'Aeons of light' are heavenly societies; 'aeons of greatness' are the infinite states within the Divine itself.
entries.notes: The text speaks of 'fourteen great aeons of light' corresponding to fourteen states of divine wisdom. The 'new aeon' is the regenerated state of the church. Aeons are not periods of time but spiritual states defined by their ruling love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing doctrinal form — a vessel of truth or good that carries spiritual life through successive states
entries.definition: Ships correspond to doctrinal forms because, as a ship carries passengers across the sea, doctrine carries the understanding through the expanse of natural knowledge. The ship of living fire is the doctrine of love; the ship of living waters is the doctrine of truth.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: Too specific to one context — 'ship' consistently denotes the doctrinal vessel, which varies in content (fire/water) depending on what it conveys.

entries.notes: Two great ships: of the day (love) and of the night (truth/faith). Each has three thrones — three governing principles. The ships 'sail' — doctrine moves through natural knowledge. Their doors open and close to receive purified light and expel waste.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A discrete degree of the understanding — a rational structure that separates interior from exterior states
entries.definition: Firmaments correspond to discrete degrees of the rational mind because, as the firmament separates waters above from waters below, each degree of understanding separates higher truths from lower. The ten firmaments are the ten planes of spiritual order.
entries.notes: The Living Spirit constructed ten firmaments. Rulers are bound 'in the firmaments' — dominant falsities restrained within rational structures. The doors of the firmaments open for the Ambassador's influx and close behind it — each degree receives and passes on the divine proceeding.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The providential cycle of spiritual reformation — the ordered revolution of knowledges and states through which the mind is progressively purified
entries.definition: The wheel corresponds to the cycle of providence because, as the wheel revolves and brings different points to prominence, the cycle of spiritual states revolves through the mind, bringing different knowledges and affections into view for purification. Evil is bound upon it, unable to comprehend its own position.
entries.notes: Contains twelve seals — truths of faith in completeness. The wheel has no root in the natural mind but gained authority through the fall of evil's concupiscence upon it. The wheel does not sever the conduits of influx because spiritual substance self-heals. A 'great mirror' — capacity for self-reflection through divine truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The natural mind — the ground of reception in which spiritual seeds are planted
entries.opposite_sense: Land of darkness — the natural mind wholly given to falsity
entries.definition: Earth corresponds to the natural mind because, as natural earth is the ground in which seeds grow, the natural mind is the ground in which truths from the Divine are received and grow into perception. 'Good earth' is the mind receptive to the Divine; 'bad earth' is the mind receptive only to evil.
entries.notes: Three earths correspond to three degrees of the natural mind. The 'new earth of light' is the regenerated natural mind. Four mountains and three vessels surround the earths — elevated states of good and containing forms encompass the natural mind. Three earths are 'toiled over' — regeneration requires labor.

entries.spiritual_meaning: An elevated state of love or perception — a state of celestial good that rises above the general plane of the mind
entries.opposite_sense: Mountains of Darkness — states of self-exaltation in falsity
entries.definition: Mountains correspond to elevated states of love because, as mountains rise above the surrounding terrain, states of celestial love rise above the general level of the natural mind. Four mountains around the earth are four elevated states of good encompassing the natural degree.
entries.notes: The 'black mountain near the sunrise' is self-intelligence persisting near the source of illumination. Mountains where 'no fruit sprouts' are states of pride where no good works arise. 'Mountains and hills' in the light-earth are elevated states of love within the Divine kingdom.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A containing form of reception — a doctrinal structure that holds and conveys spiritual content
entries.opposite_sense: Dark vessel — a containing form emptied of life
entries.definition: Vessels correspond to containing forms because, as natural vessels hold and preserve their contents, doctrinal forms hold and preserve the truths and goods they are designed to contain. The three vessels surrounding the universe are three encompassing doctrinal structures.
entries.notes: Three vessels of evil (water, darkness, fire) were expelled from the interiors through the natural mind to the outermost hells — the process of vastation. The chapter on the three vessels teaches that evils must be brought into conscious awareness before they can be removed — a core Swedenborgian doctrine.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A divine restraint upon evil — the constraining truth that holds falsity and self-love within appointed bounds
entries.opposite_sense: Bondage imposed by evil upon good — the captivity of wisdom within falsity
entries.definition: Bonds correspond to divine restraints because, as chains confine what is dangerous, truths of divine order confine evil within its appointed state. The 'lump' is the ultimate consolidated mass of evil bound forever. The 'seal' is a confirming truth that makes the restraint permanent.
entries.notes: The text distinguishes between bonds imposed by the Divine upon evil (good) and bonds imposed by evil upon the living soul (bad). The eternal chain at the end is the permanent separation of evil from good. Twelve seals in the wheel — completeness of restraining truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The intermediate sphere — the boundary between interior and exterior degrees where spiritual combat and purification occur
entries.definition: The zone corresponds to the intermediate state between the celestial and the natural — the world of spirits in Swedenborg's terminology — because it is the region where the mixed condition of good and evil is progressively resolved through separation and judgment.
entries.notes: The Ambassador is 'king of the zone.' Fifteen paths exist in the zone: four pure, eight mixed, three leading to hell. The zone is where transmigrations occur — successive changes of state. Five great camps exist in the zone, governed by five sons of the Living Spirit.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A governing principle of spiritual authority — a seat of divine power at a specific degree of the mind
entries.opposite_sense: Thrones of darkness — seats of evil's dominion
entries.definition: Thrones correspond to governing principles because, as a throne is the seat from which a king exercises authority, each spiritual throne is the principle from which divine order governs a specific domain of the mind or spiritual world.
entries.notes: Eighteen thrones total: nine in the inner aeons and nine in the zone. The arrangement maps the complete spiritual government from the Divine itself down to the apostolic function in natural life. The ninth throne in each set represents the outermost governing principle of its domain.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A passage between discrete degrees — an opening of reception through which influx enters or exits the mind
entries.definition: Gates correspond to passages of reception because, as gates control who enters a city, the mind's openings control what truths and goods are admitted. Four gates open in each world — four modes of reception at each degree.
entries.notes: The gates of the firmaments open before the Ambassador's image and close behind — each degree receives influx and passes it on. The gates of the body correspond to the senses. Evil guards the gates — ruling affections control what enters the mind. When the Light Mind enters, it takes the 'bolts' from the gates.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A pathway of influx between discrete degrees — the channel through which spiritual life flows from interior to exterior states and back
entries.definition: Conduits correspond to pathways of influx because they are the channels through which the life of love and wisdom flows between degrees of the mind — from celestial to natural and back. Three great conduits connect the entire spiritual world.
entries.notes: Three conduits: (1) celestial powers to their corporeal forms; (2) doctrinal structures to perceptions; (3) rational loves to proprial will. The wheel does not sever the conduits because spiritual substance is self-healing. Evil can flow down through conduits as well as good flowing up.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The fully realized form of the regenerated Grand Man — the ultimate collective human form in which all redeemed good and truth are gathered
entries.definition: The Last Statue corresponds to the completed regenerated human form because it is the final gathering of all scattered goods and truths into one perfect image — the Grand Man (Maximus Homo) of Swedenborg's doctrine, ascending at the consummation of all spiritual states.
entries.notes: The Statue is 'sculpted' from the remnant of all things — formed from whatever good and truth remain after the final separation. Its ascent marks the end of all spiritual epochs. The counsel of life (summons and obedience) gathers itself and sculpts itself into this form.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The ruling love — the governing principle from which all other faculties depend
entries.definition: The head corresponds to the ruling love because, as the head governs the body and all limbs depend from it, the ruling love governs the whole person and all subordinate affections depend from it. If the ruling love is destroyed, the entire spiritual life perishes.
entries.notes: The text explicitly teaches the analogy: 'as the root of all limbs hangs upon the head, so should one limb be cut off while the head exists he has hope — but if his head be cut off, the entire body dies.' The King of Darkness's lion head = lust for dominion.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will — the interior seat of love from which all spiritual life proceeds
entries.definition: The heart corresponds to the will because, as the heart is the central organ sustaining all bodily life, the will is the central faculty sustaining all spiritual life. The 'counsel of the heart' is like a king whose advisors are the faculties of the mind.
entries.notes: The heart accords to the 'wheel of the rotating sphere' in the body-cosmos correspondence — the will is the living center around which all states revolve. The heart has 'two eyes' — interior perception of the will.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The faculty of intellectual sight — the understanding's capacity to perceive spiritual truth
entries.definition: Eyes correspond to intellectual sight because, as the natural eye perceives physical objects through light, the spiritual eye perceives spiritual realities through divine wisdom. The two eyes correspond to the two light-givers (sun and moon) — love and faith.
entries.notes: The eyes have internal storehouses — memory of everything perceived. The pupil perceives by day but not by night — the understanding perceives in states of illumination but not in states of darkness. The face reflected upside-down in water is a key teaching on the inversion of spiritual perception in the natural mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A particular faculty of spiritual life — a derivative capacity proceeding from the ruling love
entries.definition: Limbs correspond to spiritual faculties because, as bodily limbs are the instruments through which the person acts, spiritual faculties are the instruments through which the ruling love operates in the mind.
entries.notes: The text names five limbs of both the good and bad trees: consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. These are five ascending degrees of spiritual reception. Each limb has a cosmic counterpart — the body-cosmos correspondence pervades the text.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The external natural person — the outermost containment of spiritual life in corporeal and sensory form
entries.definition: The body corresponds to the external person because, as the body is the outermost form in which the soul operates in the natural world, the external person is the outermost degree of the mind through which the interior spiritual life expresses itself.
entries.notes: The text explicitly teaches that the body corresponds to the whole spiritual universe: head to garments, neck to firmaments, heart to wheel, etc. 'This small body corresponds to the macro-cosmos.' The body has four worlds with seven rulers each.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A perception rooted in its ground — a system of understanding that produces works according to its quality
entries.definition: Trees correspond to perceptions because, as a tree is rooted in its soil and produces fruit according to its nature, a perception is rooted in its ground (good or evil) and produces works accordingly. The good tree is rooted in wisdom; the bad tree in self-intelligence.
entries.notes: Five trees of darkness produced from five dark elements. The teaching's core imperative is discrimination between the two trees. 'Whoever can separate them may go up to the aeon of light.' The tree is the second conduit — perceptions connected to doctrinal forms above.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Works — the spiritual productions that proceed from perception and manifest its quality
entries.definition: Fruit corresponds to works because, as fruit is what a tree produces and by which its nature is known, works are what perceptions produce and by which their spiritual quality is disclosed.
entries.notes: The teaching of error is the 'fruit' of the bad tree. The fourth stage of evil's propagation is evil fruits from the five perverted perceptions. Good fruit comes only from the tree of life planted after the bad trees are uprooted.

entries.spiritual_meaning: An interior truth in its seminal state — a truth capable of producing spiritual growth when planted in receptive good
entries.definition: Seeds correspond to interior truths in seminal form because, as seeds contain the whole potential of the plant within them and grow when planted in good soil, interior truths contain the whole potential of spiritual perception and grow when received into a will open to the Divine.
entries.notes: Seed grain and barley grain are formed and nourished by the five elements — interior truths are developed through five spiritual faculties. Frost, hail, and snow destroy seed-corn — frozen falsity destroys truths capable of producing good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: External truth clothing interior good — the outermost form of truth that covers, protects, and makes interior states presentable
entries.opposite_sense: Rags — degraded and devastated truths stripped of their living quality
entries.definition: Garments correspond to external truths because, as garments clothe and protect the body, truths clothe and protect the goods of the will. 'Light garments' are truths woven from wisdom; 'rags' are truths that have been degraded through profanation or loss of interior good.
entries.notes: The chapter on 'names of the light' distinguishes great garments (purified truths), rags (devoured truths entangled in rulers), worn garments (truths overpowered by the proprium), and tattered clothes (three encompassing truths laid bare). All are one power separated into many conditions through the first combat.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love as the ruling good — the Lord as the source of all spiritual warmth and illumination
entries.definition: The sun corresponds to Divine Love because, as the natural sun is the source of all light and warmth sustaining life, Divine Love is the source of all wisdom and good sustaining spiritual life. The sun does seven good things — a complete set of beneficial spiritual operations.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: While the sun's light is wisdom, the sun itself — as source — corresponds to love. The text makes this explicit by associating it with the ship of living fire and distinguishing it from the moon.

entries.notes: The sun 'never wanes' — Divine Love is perpetually full, unlike the moon (faith). Three archetypes of the Father are displayed in the sun. Five archetypes occur in the sun. Two great mysteries are revealed at sunrise and sunset. The sun and moon are 'strangers' to the zodiac — Divine Good and Truth originate in the Divine, not in the natural order.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Faith — Divine Truth in reflected form, illuminating states of spiritual obscurity
entries.definition: The moon corresponds to faith because, as the moon reflects sunlight into the darkness of night, faith reflects divine love into states of spiritual obscurity. The moon waxes and wanes — faith fluctuates in the regenerating mind.
entries.notes: The ship of the moon contains the First Man — celestial good dwelling within the vessel of faith. The moon wanes unlike the sun — faith fluctuates but love does not. Moon and sun counted with the zodiac 'as a rule' but are 'strangers to them' — Divine Good and Truth govern the natural order but do not originate from it.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Knowledge of good and truth — particular truths that illuminate the understanding from the natural memory
entries.definition: Stars correspond to knowledges of good and truth because, as stars provide individual points of light in the night sky, knowledges provide individual insights in the general field of the natural understanding.
entries.notes: Stars are bound on the revolving wheel. Five stars (planets) are the five principal evil affections counterfeiting the five divine goods. Stars and zodiacal signs determine births — fixed spiritual laws govern the conditions under which minds come into being.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The twelve fundamental governing principles of the complete spiritual round — the totality of all states through which spiritual progression or regression occurs
entries.opposite_sense: Twelve signs as rulers of depravity — the counterfeit completeness of falsity from evil
entries.definition: The zodiac corresponds to the complete ordered cycle of spiritual states because its twelve signs encompass all possible conditions of the revolving natural mind. In the positive sense, they are states of spiritual progression; in the negative, they are twelve governing evils marshaled from five hells.
entries.notes: The twelve signs are mapped onto the human body from head (Aries) to feet (Pisces). Two signs per world of darkness. Arranged in four groups of three at four quarters. Twelve signs also mapped onto the body both vertically and laterally, yielding a dual system.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Celestial good — the good of the inmost heaven
entries.opposite_sense: Semblance of celestial good — the external appearance of good covering infernal evil
entries.definition: Gold corresponds to celestial good because, as gold is the most precious and incorruptible metal, celestial good is the most interior and incorruptible spiritual quality. In the negative sense, gold as the body of the King of Smoke signifies the external appearance of good covering total intellectual obscurity.
entries.notes: Gold is the body of Smoke's rulers — the deepest deception is evil that clothes itself in the semblance of the highest good. The correspondence is precisely Swedenborgian: gold = celestial good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual truth — truth belonging to the spiritual degree
entries.opposite_sense: Falsified truth — truth perverted to serve evil
entries.definition: Silver corresponds to spiritual truth because, as silver is the second most precious metal reflecting light clearly, spiritual truth is the quality that reflects divine wisdom in the spiritual degree. As the body of Water's rulers, silver = falsified truth.
entries.notes: Silver is the body of rulers belonging to the world of Water — falsified truth is the external form of the concupiscence that perverts genuine truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Natural good — the good of the lowest or natural degree
entries.opposite_sense: Perverted natural good — natural good serving self-love
entries.definition: Copper corresponds to natural good because, as copper is useful and warm-colored but less precious than gold, natural good is genuine but exterior. As the body of Fire's rulers, copper = perverted natural good.
entries.notes: Copper is the body of rulers belonging to the world of Fire — self-love perverts natural good into its instrument.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Natural truth in its hardened, unyielding form
entries.opposite_sense: Hardened natural falsity — impenetrable resistance to divine truth
entries.definition: Iron corresponds to hardened natural truth because, as iron is hard, strong, and resistant, natural truth in its lowest form is hard and unyielding. As the body of Wind's rulers, iron = hardened falsity impervious to truth.
entries.notes: The King of Darkness is 'harder than iron' — ruling evil is more impenetrable than any truth or argument. Iron implements cannot pierce him — no instrument of natural truth can penetrate consolidated evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Dense base falsity — the heaviest, most inert form of falsity
entries.definition: Lead corresponds to the densest and basest falsity because, as lead is the heaviest common metal, lacking luster and easily corroded, base falsity is the heaviest spiritual substance, lacking any reflection of truth.
entries.notes: Lead and tin are the body of rulers belonging to the world of Darkness — the deepest hells clothe themselves in the densest falsity. Tin adds counterfeit truth to the base falsity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The lust for dominion from self-love — the predatory desire to rule over all
entries.definition: The lion corresponds to the lust for dominion because, as the lion is the most powerful and domineering predator, the love of dominion from self-love is the most powerful and domineering of all evil affections — it seeks to devour and subject all other affections.
entries.notes: The lion-face is the head of the King of Darkness and the ruling love of the world of Fire. Consistently represents the lust for dominion — the foremost of all evil affections.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Predatory rationality — reasoning from falsity that seizes and elevates itself above truth
entries.definition: The eagle corresponds to predatory rationality because, as the eagle soars high and seizes prey from above, false reasoning elevates itself and seizes truths from their proper place, perverting them to serve self-love.
entries.notes: Eagle-faced = shoulders/wings of the King of Darkness, and the ruling love of the world of Wind. The power to rise and seize = the intellectual capacity to elevate reasoning from falsity above genuine truth.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The falsification of truth — the ruling evil that destroys truth by distorting it from within
entries.definition: The dragon corresponds to the falsification of truth because, as a dragon is a monstrous serpent that devours, the falsification of truth is a monstrous spiritual power that swallows genuine truth and converts it into its opposite.
entries.notes: Dragon-faced = belly of the King of Darkness, and the ruling love of the world of pure Darkness. The 'dragon with fourteen heads' in the body is the self-derived thinking of the proprium with fourteen powers of dominion (seven interior faculties + seven exterior). Five dens = five hidden recesses of the natural mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Base corporeal knowing — the lowest form of natural perception perverted to infernal ends
entries.definition: The fish corresponds to base corporeal knowing because, as fish dwell in the lowest waters, the most external sensory knowledge dwells in the lowest degree of the natural mind. When perverted, it serves the hells.
entries.notes: Fish-faced = tail of the King of Darkness, and the ruling love of the world of Water. The ultimate sensory expression of evil. Rulers are 'caught like fish in the sea' — natural knowledge is seized from the waters of the external mind.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A precious interior truth of faith — a truth of great spiritual value drawn from the general body of knowledge
entries.definition: The pearl corresponds to a precious truth because, as a pearl is formed within a shell in the sea and must be drawn up, the most precious truths are formed within general natural knowledge and must be drawn forth through spiritual labor.
entries.notes: The First Man is raised from the contest 'as a pearl is brought up from the sea' — the celestial state of innocence drawn from the overwhelming mass of natural knowledge.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The perception of spiritual good — the sphere of celestial delight perceived as an interior pleasantness
entries.opposite_sense: Stench/putridity — the perception of spiritual evil
entries.definition: Perfume corresponds to the perception of spiritual good because, as fragrance is perceived without direct contact and fills an entire space, the perception of good from heaven pervades the whole mind without material cause.
entries.notes: The second of the five divine emanations from the Father. 'Sweet perfume that takes away all affliction' = the celestial delight that removes all spiritual suffering.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The mode of spiritual appropriation — the quality by which goods and truths are received into the life
entries.definition: Taste corresponds to the mode of appropriation because, as taste determines how food is received by the body, the quality of spiritual delight determines how truths and goods are received into the life of the will.
entries.notes: Five tastes mapped to five dark worlds: salty (Smoke), sour (Fire), sharp (Wind), sweet-deceptive (Water), bitter (Darkness). Each taste reveals the quality of the evil: salty = craving for conjunction of evil with falsity; bitter = interior torment of unmixed evil.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The understanding — the intellectual, active, and discerning aspect of the mind
entries.definition: Male corresponds to the understanding because, as the male principle is active and generative outwardly, the understanding is the faculty that actively discerns, thinks, and generates ideas from the truths it receives.

variant_readings.reason_not_chosen: The male/female pair most consistently maps to understanding/will throughout, not to active/receptive will.

entries.notes: Male and female together = the complete person. The upper side of creation is male (interior = understanding); the lower side is female (exterior = will). Ten parts: five male, five female = ten aspects of the mind. The two ascendants (fire/lust) are the 'father and mother' of all these.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will — the receptive, volitional, and affective aspect of the mind
entries.definition: Female corresponds to the will because, as the female principle is receptive and generative inwardly, the will is the faculty that receives good, nurtures affections, and produces the interior life of love.
entries.notes: In the final separation, 'male will be divided from female' = the understanding that served evil will be separated from the will of evil. Matter herself is female — the proprium is the receptive, generative origin of all evil forms.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual combat — temptation and the conflict between good and evil within the mind
entries.definition: War corresponds to spiritual combat because, as natural war is the clash of opposing forces, spiritual combat is the clash of truth against falsity and good against evil within the regenerating mind. Every war in the text is a temptation-combat.
entries.notes: Five great wars correspond to five stages of the Lord's redemptive combat. The sons of light wage five combats against the sons of darkness. Three great blows are struck against the enemy. Every descent of a divine figure is followed by combat.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The separation of good from evil and truth from falsity — the progressive freeing of wisdom from its admixture with the proprium
entries.definition: Purification corresponds to the separation of good from evil because, as natural purification removes impurities from a substance, spiritual purification removes the falsities and evils of self-love from the good and truth held captive within the mind.
entries.notes: Purification proceeds through the sun and moon — through divine love and faith. The Ambassador purifies by his image. The three vessels are purified by being brought to consciousness and then expelled — the core doctrine that evil must be seen before it can be removed.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Elevation to interior states — the movement of good and truth from the natural toward the celestial degree
entries.opposite_sense: Descent — the movement from interior to exterior, either as influx or as fall
entries.definition: Ascent corresponds to elevation toward interior states because, as rising is movement from lower to higher, spiritual ascent is the movement of the mind from exterior natural states toward interior celestial states — closer to conjunction with the Divine.
entries.notes: The First Man's ascent from the abyss = the restoration of celestial good after temptation. The Last Statue ascends at the end. The light is gathered 'from below to above' through three conduits. The progression is: fire→wind→water→light→air upward through degrees.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The commingling of good with evil — the state of the unregenerate mind where truth and falsity are intertwined
entries.opposite_sense: Separation — the distinguishing of good from evil
entries.definition: Mixing corresponds to the commingling of good with evil because the core condition of the fallen mind is that divine wisdom has been intertwined with falsity from self-love, and both exist together in the same faculties until regeneration separates them.
entries.notes: The entire cosmic drama is precipitated by the mixing of light with darkness and resolved by their final separation. The 'mixed state' is the condition of all life between the first combat and the Last Statue. The person who cannot separate the two falls into death.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The forming of spiritual states — the shaping of interior conditions into determinate forms of good or evil
entries.definition: Sculpting corresponds to forming spiritual states because, as a sculptor gives determinate shape to formless material, the divine or infernal powers give determinate form to the amorphous potential of the mind.
entries.notes: Matter is the 'chief sculptor' — the proprium gives form to evil. The Last Statue is 'sculpted' — the regenerated human is formed. The builder analogy describes the Living Spirit as both architect and carpenter. The sea giant is sculpted by its own lust.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The active divine operation of seeking and reclaiming scattered goods and truths from their captivity in falsity
entries.opposite_sense: Infernal hunting — ensnaring and retaining spiritual life in bondage to evil
entries.definition: Hunting corresponds to the active reclaiming of scattered good because, as a hunter pursues and captures prey through skill, the Divine pursues and reclaims the good and truth held captive in the power of evil, drawing them forth through wisdom.
entries.notes: Four divine hunters and four infernal hunters in symmetry. The net = encompassing truth or deceptive falsity. The sea = the field of operation. The ship = the vessel in which the hunter operates. A key structural chapter showing the complete symmetry of redemptive and destructive operations.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Interior rest — the state of the will when goods and truths are conjoined and all internal conflict ceases
entries.opposite_sense: Fear/trembling — the dread and agitation of evil when exposed to divine order
entries.definition: Peace corresponds to interior rest because, as peace is the cessation of external warfare, spiritual peace is the cessation of all internal conflict between good and evil — the state of the will resting in conjunction with the Divine.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries/signs of the First Man. The peace given in descent is 'the same' as in ascent — divine conjunction is unbroken through temptation. Peace is the first of the five lessons proclaimed in the world. The 'chain of peace' binds the regenerated person.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Communicated divine power — the transmission of authority and strength from one degree to another
entries.definition: The right hand corresponds to communicated divine power because, as the right hand extends strength and aid, the divine power extends its strength from one degree to another — from the Divine to the celestial will, and from the rescuing truth to the restored good.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries/signs. Given twice: at the descent into combat and at the ascent from it. The angel who holds the victory prize 'extends the right hand' to the departing soul.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The conjunction of affections — the union of love with love, or truth with good, in mutual delight
entries.definition: The kiss corresponds to the conjunction of affections because, as a kiss is the most intimate outward expression of love, spiritual conjunction is the inmost union of will with will — the meeting of divine love with human love in mutual delight.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries/signs. The Mother of Life embraces the First Man at departure — divine wisdom conjoins with celestial good before combat. Given again at the ascent — conjunction restored.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Humble acknowledgment of the Divine — the will's act of bowing before what is above it in spiritual order
entries.definition: The salutation corresponds to humble acknowledgment because, as making obeisance is the outward expression of reverence toward one greater, the spiritual salutation is the will's interior bowing before the Divine in acknowledgment of its dependence.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries/signs. The First Man bows to the God of truth — the celestial will acknowledges the supreme Divine. Given at both descent and ascent.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The transmission of interior authority — the communication of divine power and governance from a higher to a lower degree
entries.definition: The laying on of hands corresponds to the transmission of interior authority because, as the physical act confers power and office, the spiritual act communicates the capacity to govern and lead from one degree of the mind to another.
entries.notes: One of the five mysteries/signs. The Mother of Life lays hands on the First Man — divine wisdom communicates governing authority to celestial good. The second laying on of hands makes him 'leader of his brethren in the new aeon.'

entries.spiritual_meaning: The endless revolving of the unregenerate soul through successive states of falsity — passage from one false appearance to another without reaching truth
entries.definition: Transmigration corresponds to the endless cycling through false states because, as the soul is said to pass from body to body, the unregenerate mind passes from one false persuasion to another, never finding rest in truth.
entries.notes: The guidance of the bad tree is transmigration — endless revolving in falsity. One of the eight mixed paths leads to transmigration. 'Restored' wisdom is that which went through transmigration and was reclaimed.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Divine calling — the influx of divine truth that awakens and calls the captive will to ascend toward the Divine
entries.definition: The summons corresponds to the divine calling because, as a summons calls a person to appear, the divine calling is the influx of truth from the Lord that reaches into the captive human spirit and calls it upward toward conjunction with the Divine.
entries.notes: Always paired with 'obedience' (the response). Together they constitute the twelfth judge, the counsel of life, and a key structural element of the five-fold system. The summons descends headlong — divine truth enters the lowest states with its highest aspect first (the inversion teaching).

entries.spiritual_meaning: The will's receptive response to the divine calling — the reciprocal acknowledgment and willing reception of divine truth
entries.definition: Obedience corresponds to the will's reception because, as obedience is the response to a command, spiritual obedience is the will's free and willing reception of truth from the Lord, completing the circuit of influx and return.
entries.notes: The obedience ascends in response to the summons that descends. Together they are counted as two among the twelve (making the ten sons into twelve). The obedience 'ascends with its inmost things foremost' — the will responds from its deepest love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Conjunction — the union of will and understanding, good and truth, love and wisdom in their mutual complementarity
entries.opposite_sense: Division — the separation of what should be conjoined
entries.definition: Two signifies conjunction because all spiritual reality exists in pairs that must be united: will and understanding, good and truth, love and wisdom. The number two expresses the duality that seeks unity.
entries.notes: Two essences (light/darkness), two ships (sun/moon), two light-givers, two deaths, two sons of the First Man (will and understanding that 'make four'), two eyes of the body as two ships. The two ascendants are fire and lust — the father and mother (active/receptive evil).

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness as to truth in its discrete degrees — completeness of proceeding from inmost to outmost
entries.definition: Three signifies fullness as to discrete degrees because the Divine proceeds through three essential planes: celestial, spiritual, and natural. Everything in the text that comes in threes expresses this threefold completeness of proceeding.
entries.notes: Three earths = three degrees of natural mind. Three vessels = three containing forms. Three emanations from the Father. Three seasons of cosmic time. Three blows against the enemy. Three rocks. Three images in the elect person (spiritual, psychic, corporeal). Three conduits. Three entreaties. Three great days.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness as to manifestation — the complete set of faculties through which spiritual life is made operative in the created order
entries.definition: Five signifies fullness of manifestation because the spiritual mind operates through five essential faculties (perception, understanding, thought, will, and action). Every set of five in the text represents the complete set of operative spiritual capacities at a given degree.
entries.notes: The most architecturally significant number. Five elements of light and five of darkness. Five limbs of both trees. Five fathers proceeding from one another. Five wars, five releases, five greatnesses, five signs/mysteries. Five sons of First Man + five sons of Living Spirit = ten. Five storehouses, five worlds, five kings, five spirits, five bodies, five tastes. Five dens of the dragon. Five archetypes in the sun.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Holy fullness — completeness of a spiritual process from beginning to end
entries.definition: Seven signifies holy fullness because a complete spiritual process — from its inception through its fulfillment — passes through seven states. Five interior faculties plus the summons and obedience = seven, constituting a holy completeness.
entries.notes: Seven works of the Living Spirit. Seven firmaments under the King of Honour. Seven rivers flowing into each ruler. Seven good things the sun does daily. Seven evil things night does. Seven rulers in each of four worlds of the body. Seven hostels for the rebels. Five + two (summons and obedience) = seven.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of truth in all its degrees — the completeness of remains or of operative truth through every plane
entries.definition: Ten signifies fullness of truth through every plane because it represents the complete set of derivative truths and goods spanning all degrees of the mind. Five sons of the First Man + five sons of the Living Spirit = ten operative truths.
entries.notes: Ten firmaments. Ten vehicles of Jesus. Ten works of the Ambassador. Ten parts (5 male + 5 female). Four greatnesses 'appointed to ten parts.' The text explicitly derives ten from 5+5 in several places.

entries.spiritual_meaning: All things of faith and the church in their completeness — the total complement of goods and truths proceeding from the Divine
entries.opposite_sense: Twelve darkened — the counterfeit completeness of falsity marshaled against the Divine
entries.definition: Twelve signifies all things of faith in completeness because it represents the full circle of spiritual truth in all its aspects. The twelve hours of each day are the twelve complete qualities of that state of illumination.
entries.notes: Twelve hours of four days. Twelve hours of four nights. Twelve judges. Twelve seals in the wheel. Twelve signs of the zodiac. Twelve spirits of error. Ten + two (summons and obedience) = twelve. In its negative sense: twelve rulers of depravity fashioned from five hells.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Conjunction in completeness — fullness in all four directions or orientations of the spiritual mind
entries.definition: Four signifies conjunction in completeness because it represents the full compass of spiritual orientation — the four cardinal directions in which the mind can receive and express the Divine. What is extended to four sides is universally operative.
entries.notes: Four days and four nights. Four hunters of light and four of darkness. Four mountains encompassing the earth. Four walls surrounding the vessels. Four worlds in the body. Four great domains of the spiritual order. Three distributed 'three by three' to 'four climes.'

entries.spiritual_meaning: Complete fullness of spiritual operation — the total complement of divine faculties in their conjugial union (seven times two)
entries.opposite_sense: Fourteen heads of the dragon — the full dominion of the self-derived proprium
entries.definition: Fourteen signifies complete fullness of spiritual operation because it is seven (holy fullness) multiplied by two (conjunction), expressing the total complement of divine faculties in their conjoined operation. The fourteen aeons of light are the complete states of divine wisdom.
entries.notes: Fourteen great aeons of light: 5+2+5+2 = 14. The dragon's fourteen heads: 7 interior + 7 exterior faculties of the proprium. The number appears precisely where the text describes the total operative system of either divine or infernal governance.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Completeness of covering or governance — the full set of governing principles encompassing both interior and exterior degrees (nine times two)
entries.definition: Eighteen signifies completeness of governance because it is nine (the fullness of judgment or ordering at one side) doubled to encompass both sides: nine thrones in the interior heavens and nine in the zone of spiritual conflict.
entries.notes: Eighteen thrones: 9 inner + 9 outer. Eighteen garments around the child in the womb: 9 of the child + 9 of the mother. The number expresses the mirrored structure of governance between interior and exterior orders.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of spiritual faculties in their complete internal articulation — five times five, signifying that each of the five essential faculties contains within itself the full five
entries.definition: Twenty-five signifies the complete internal articulation of the five faculties because each of the five essential faculties of the spiritual mind contains within itself all five, yielding twenty-five — the total operative capacity of the regenerating mind.
entries.notes: Explicitly derived in the text: 'five powers in each of five garments, five times five is their number.' The summons and obedience constitute the twenty-five with their twenty-five limbs — the complete system of divine calling and human reception.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of spiritual pathways in manifestation — three times five, signifying the complete complement of operative ways across all three degrees
entries.definition: Fifteen signifies the complete set of pathways in the intermediate state because it combines three (discrete degrees) with five (full manifestation), yielding fifteen distinct ways through which the mixed state resolves into good, evil, or continued mixture.
entries.notes: Fifteen paths in the zone: 4 pure + 8 mixed + 3 leading to hell. The distribution reflects the text's teaching that the paths of regeneration vastly outnumber the paths of damnation, while the mixed paths exceed both.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual life — the state of continuous reception of love and wisdom from the Divine into the will and understanding
entries.opposite_sense: Death — the state of refusal of divine influx, where the spirit subsists in its own darkness
entries.definition: Life corresponds to spiritual life because genuine life is not biological existence but the continuous reception of the Divine into the interiors of the mind. The 'living soul' is the divine good dispersed within creation, held captive and awaiting liberation.
entries.notes: The 'living soul' is the central object of all cosmic drama — the divine good entrapped in the natural order. Life and light are always paired — good and truth together. The 'counsel of life' gathers all lives at the end.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Spiritual death — the state of separation from the Divine, where the spirit exists only in self-love and falsity
entries.opposite_sense: Spiritual life
entries.definition: Death corresponds to the state of separation from the Divine because spiritual death is not cessation of existence but the state in which the will turns wholly away from the Lord and subsists solely in self-love and its falsities.
entries.notes: Two great deaths: the first is temporal (good mixed with evil until purification), the second is eternal (permanent separation from the Divine). The five elements of death mirror the five of life. Matter is called 'thought of death.' The second death is the profoundest teaching of the text.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine Love itself — the essential nature of the Divine as self-giving good
entries.opposite_sense: Hate — the primal spiritual death that seeks to destroy all that belongs to another
entries.definition: Love is defined by the text itself as the Father of Greatness — the Divine giving itself for everything. Hate is the first death that seeks to ruin even what is not its own. Love and hate are the two fundamental principles underlying all spiritual reality.
entries.notes: The text's own definition: 'Love is the Father who dwells in his glorious land. The entirety of the divine has been revealed therein. These two are a single living body, the Father and his love.' Hate is 'the first death that welled up' — evil's essential nature is envy and hatred of all good.

natural_variants: lust for what is not one's own
entries.spiritual_meaning: The lust to appropriate what belongs to the Divine — the fundamental impulse of self-love to usurp and possess spiritual goods that do not belong to it
entries.definition: Envy corresponds to the fundamental evil impulse because it is the desire to possess and control what belongs to another — specifically, the proprium's desire to seize and dominate the goods and truths that belong only to the Divine. It is the origin of all spiritual warfare.
entries.notes: The text describes three acts of envy: envying the light, envying the Ambassador's image, envying Adam. Each represents a successive stage of evil's usurpation. 'The entirety of envy is this first nature that occurred in the worlds of darkness' — the proprium itself.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The Most Ancient Church — the earliest celestial state of humanity, and specifically the natural will and understanding formed in the divine image
entries.definition: Adam corresponds to the Most Ancient Church because the text's Adam is not merely a biological figure but the primordial human form created in the image of the Divine — the earliest state in which divine good and truth were received and reflected in natural human faculties.
entries.notes: Adam was fashioned by the rulers after the image of the Ambassador — the proprium shaped the natural human in a counterfeit likeness of the Divine. Three qualities distinguish Adam: the divine image, the arrangement of the five elements, and the seal of all powers. Seven reasons the rulers made Adam.

entries.spiritual_meaning: An interior repository of the mind — a hidden memory-store or containing state where goods, truths, evils, or falsities are preserved
entries.definition: Storehouses correspond to interior repositories because, as storehouses preserve what is deposited in them, the interior states of the mind preserve the goods, truths, evils, and falsities that have been received and appropriated through life.
entries.notes: Five storehouses of darkness = five repositories of fundamental evil. Hidden storehouses of the Father = the innermost degrees of the Divine. Each sensory faculty has its own storehouses — memory-stores for sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. The heart's storehouse rules over all others.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The one who communicates Divine Truth directly into the natural mind — the apostolic function of teaching and transmission
entries.definition: The Apostle of Light corresponds to the specific function of communicating divine truth into natural life because, as an apostle is sent to deliver a message, this spiritual capacity is the means by which interior truth reaches the external person.
entries.notes: The first power summoned by the Light Mind. The ninth throne is assigned to the apostle — the outermost governing principle in the zone of spiritual conflict. The apostle's 'counterpart' companion corresponds to the companion perception that aids spiritual teaching.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Pristine — wisdom that has never been contaminated by self-love or falsity from evil
entries.definition: What is virginal corresponds to pristine wisdom because, as virginity signifies untouched purity, pristine wisdom is truth that has never descended into the combat of temptation or been contaminated by the proprium.
entries.notes: Distinguished from 'continent' (restored). Assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness — the infinite states of the Divine. The Light Mind assuming the forms of the elect is called 'virginal.' In the natural person: one who has never conjoined understanding with self-love.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Restored — wisdom that was contaminated through mixture with falsity but has been purified and returned to a holy state
entries.definition: What is continent corresponds to restored wisdom because, as continence signifies self-mastery after prior indulgence, restored wisdom is truth that descended into the mixed state, was purified from its contamination, and returned to holiness.
entries.notes: The remainder of light that went through transmigration and was reclaimed. The new man purified from the old man is 'continent.' In the natural person: one who was conjoined with worldly affection but purified himself from it.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Blessedness — the reception of Divine Good into the inmost will
entries.definition: Happiness corresponds to blessedness because true happiness is the state of the will when it receives and is filled with divine good — the inmost delight of conjunction with the Lord.
entries.notes: One of the three divine attributes present at every plane: happiness, wisdom, and power. In the first greatness, happiness is the Father himself. In the sun, it is the Living Spirit. In the moon, the Mind of the Father. In the elements, the Pillar of Glory.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Illumination — the reception of Divine Truth that enlightens the understanding
entries.definition: Wisdom corresponds to illumination because true wisdom is the state of the understanding when it receives and is filled with divine truth — the perception of spiritual reality as it truly is.
entries.notes: The second of three divine attributes at every plane. In the first greatness, wisdom is the Great Spirit. In the sun, the Mother of Life. In the moon, the Virgin of Light. In the elements, the five sons of the Living Spirit.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Efficacy — the conjunction of good and truth in act, producing spiritual use and effect
entries.definition: Power corresponds to efficacy because true spiritual power is not force but the conjunction of good and truth in their operation — the capacity to produce genuine spiritual effects and uses.
entries.notes: The third divine attribute at every plane. In the first greatness, power is all the gods and angels. In the sun, the Living Spirit. In the moon, all gods and angels within. In the elements, the five sons of the First Man.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Divine good — a celestial good proceeding from the Divine Love
entries.definition: The term 'god' when used of plural divine beings corresponds to celestial goods — particular goods of love that have been called forth from the Divine itself and established in the form of the Divine's own goodness.
entries.notes: Three archetypes: gods, rich ones, and angels. 'Gods' are the first emanations summoned by the Father. 'Rich ones' are derivative truths proceeding from those goods. 'Angels' are the receptive forms through which both operate. The system operates at three levels: eternal, redemptive, and governmental.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Abundance of truth — derivative truths proceeding from celestial goods
entries.definition: The 'rich ones' correspond to abundances of truth because, as the rich possess material wealth in abundance, these beings possess spiritual truth in abundance — they are the secondary emanations that proceed from the primary goods.
entries.notes: Belong to the household of the Ambassador — truth's mediating function. Called 'rich' because truth derived from good is inexhaustible in its forms and applications.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Receptive form of wisdom — a truth-bearing form through which divine good and truth are received, transmitted, and made operative
entries.definition: Angels correspond to receptive forms of wisdom because, as angels serve as messengers between the Divine and the human, these spiritual forms are the means through which divine good and truth are communicated to lower degrees and made operative in them.
entries.notes: Belong to the household of the Beloved of the Lights. Three angels accompany the Light Form at death: one bearing the prize, one the garment, one the crown. Angels are sent to seize rulers — divine truths pursue and restrain evil affections.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The composite selfhood formed from the accumulated residue of all spiritual states — the monstrous aggregate of natural falsities consolidated from the refuse of spiritual purification
entries.definition: The sea giant corresponds to the composite selfhood because it is formed from the accumulated residue of all spiritual states, consolidated by the force of concupiscence into a single monstrous form dwelling in the vast body of natural knowledge.
entries.notes: Discharged from the sphere into the sea. Formed by its own lust and thought from many doctrines and counsels. Serves three purposes: relieving the sphere, restraining the zodiac, and gathering all refuse. The composite falsity that rules the sensory plane.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The foundational sustaining power — the guardian principle at the lowest boundary between the spiritual world and the abyss, which upholds all things from below
entries.definition: The Porter corresponds to the foundational sustaining power because, as a porter bears burdens, this divine power bears the entire weight of the spiritual world from its lowest point, holding the boundary against the hells below.
entries.notes: Stands at the base of the Pillar of Glory. The Porter's 'footsoles' correspond to the very base of the natural person. The Living Spirit strips off its garments 'before the Porter' — the operative truth divests its external forms at the lowest boundary. The fifth watch-station.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A foundational truth — an immovable truth upon which the entire spiritual order rests
entries.definition: Rocks correspond to foundational truths because, as rocks are the most solid and enduring formations of the earth, foundational truths are the most firm and unchangeable principles of spiritual order upon which all else is built.
entries.notes: Three great rocks: the Pillar of Glory, the new earth of light, and the great thought from Jesus. Each represents a foundational truth established in a different degree. The Adamant of Light is the indestructible truth from divine good.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Obscured truth — truth that is not yet fully transparent but carries within it both good and evil awaiting separation
entries.definition: Clouds correspond to obscured truth because, as clouds carry water (truth) but obscure the sun (love), obscured truths carry within them both genuine good and captive evil that must be separated through spiritual processes.
entries.notes: Four types of clouds (fire, water, wind, light) rise from four elements toward the Virgin of Light. Each has distinctive signs and processes. The cloud of light proceeds 'in stillness and calm.' From clouds, the lives are purified and the rulers are stripped.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The warmth of love — the active quality of celestial or spiritual love
entries.opposite_sense: Coldness — the absence of all love and charity
entries.definition: Heat corresponds to love because, as warmth sustains natural life and flows from fire, the warmth of love sustains spiritual life and flows from the fire of divine love. Cold is the extinction of all charity.
entries.notes: Heat and cold are called 'the father and the mother' — the originating evil (self-love) and the originating falsity (absence of charity). The King of Darkness can alternately blaze with self-love or freeze with the extinction of charity.

entries.spiritual_meaning: The absence of all love and charity — the spiritual condition where no warmth of good remains
entries.opposite_sense: Warmth of divine love
entries.definition: Cold corresponds to the absence of charity because, as cold extinguishes natural warmth and freezes life, the absence of love from the Lord extinguishes all spiritual warmth and renders the mind inert and lifeless.
entries.notes: The King of Darkness 'sends forth frost and his entire body freezes like a mountain of snow.' Frost, hail, and snow destroy seed-corn — frozen falsity destroys interior truths. Cold is specifically the 'mother' — the receptive/volitional aspect of evil's origin.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of judgment or ordering at one side of a mirrored structure — completeness of governance in one domain
entries.definition: Nine signifies fullness of ordering at one side because the text consistently uses nine to denote one half of an eighteen-part governance structure: nine thrones in the interior heavens and nine in the zone.
entries.notes: Nine thrones in the outer aeons + nine in the zone = eighteen. Nine coverings of the child + nine of the mother = eighteen. Nine is the fullness of one domain awaiting its mirror.

entries.spiritual_meaning: A new beginning — the inauguration of a new spiritual state beyond the completeness of seven
entries.definition: Eight signifies a new beginning because, being one beyond seven (holy fullness), it marks the start of a new cycle or degree of spiritual existence. Eight places of the living fire span from the foundation to the final consummation.
entries.notes: Eight earths below (four composite + four dark). Holy living fire is present in eight places — eight states of spiritual order from the foundation beneath the light-earth to the final fire of judgment. Eight hundred and forty times ten thousand rulers in the body.

entries.spiritual_meaning: Fullness of spiritual operation in the natural degree — twelve (complete faith) times three (all degrees), or six squared signifying the fullness of natural labor
entries.definition: Thirty-six signifies the complete system of doctrinal structures in the natural degree because it combines twelve (completeness of faith) with three (all degrees) — the total number of organized truths through which derivative falsities are contained.
entries.notes: Thirty-six cities for the children of the giants. Thirty-six angels with the Youth. May also be understood as 6×6 — the fullness of natural labor (six being the number of labor).
