summary.consistency_assessment: The per-chapter spiritual readings converge well on the major cosmological entities: Father of Greatness as Divine Love, First Man as the Lord's celestial will descending into combat, Living Spirit as proceeding divine truth, and the Ambassador as mediating divine manifestation are remarkably stable throughout. The five-element system (fire/wind/water/light/air → love/influx/truth/wisdom/perception) is consistent with only minor variations in emphasis. The greatest divergence occurs in: (1) 'light' which oscillates between 'wisdom' and 'divine truth' depending on context — I resolved this toward 'wisdom' as the more encompassing reading; (2) the Living Spirit, sometimes rendered as 'Divine Providence' and sometimes as 'Divine Truth proceeding' — resolved toward the latter as his primary function; (3) 'earth' which the readings sometimes treat as the whole natural mind and sometimes as the church on earth — resolved toward 'natural mind' as the more consistent architectural reading. Numerical correspondences were the area of greatest per-chapter inconsistency, as the earlier pipeline often treated numbers as literal counts rather than spiritual qualities — I systematically corrected these based on both Swedenborg's established doctrine and the text's own internal usage patterns.
summary.five_fold_systems: The text's most distinctive architecture is its pervasive five-fold correspondence system. At least seven interlocking sets of five appear: (1) Five elements of light (fire, wind, water, light, air) = five spiritual faculties (love, influx, truth, wisdom, perception); (2) Five elements of darkness (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) = five genera of evil (intellectual obscurity, self-love, false persuasion, corrupted truth, total privation); (3) Five limbs of the good tree (consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind) = five ascending degrees of spiritual reception (outermost reception → sustaining guidance → interior seeing → active understanding → inmost willing); (4) Five fathers proceeding from one another = five discrete degrees of divine influx from infinite love to the individual soul; (5) Five metals (gold, silver, copper, iron, lead) = five degrees of spiritual substance from celestial good to base falsity; (6) Five tastes (salty, sour, sharp, sweet, bitter) = five modes of appropriation in the infernal states; (7) Five shapes of the King of Darkness (lion, demon, eagle, dragon, fish) = five genera of organized evil (dominion, evil action, predatory reason, falsification, base sensuality). These sets interlock through their shared five-fold structure: each describes the same five-part reality from a different perspective. The five light elements correspond to the five limbs of the good tree, which correspond to the five fathers — all are the same five discrete degrees viewed as substance, faculty, and origin respectively. The twelve-fold system (5+5+2) is equally important: the twelve hours of each day and night, the twelve judges, the twelve zodiacal signs, all derive from the five sons of the First Man plus the five sons of the Living Spirit plus the summons and obedience.
summary.key_findings: Several findings emerged only through corpus-level analysis that individual chapter readings missed: (1) The 'living air' (the fifth element) is explicitly stated to be the one element that was NOT wounded in the first combat — this is the spiritual atmosphere or rational sphere that remains unpenetrated by falsity, a correspondence with profound implications; (2) The text's distinction between 'virginal' and 'continent' maps precisely to Swedenborg's distinction between the celestial church (which never fell) and the spiritual church (which fell and was restored); (3) The three conduits connecting heaven to earth form a complete anatomy of influx that closely parallels Swedenborg's doctrine of discrete degrees; (4) The teaching that evil must first be brought into conscious awareness in the natural mind before it can be removed (the chapter on the three vessels) is a strikingly precise parallel to Swedenborg's doctrine of temptation; (5) The 'inversion' teaching — that spiritual realities appear upside-down when reflected in natural truth — maps to Swedenborg's teaching about the apparent inversion between celestial and natural perspectives; (6) The text's insistence that Divine Good and Truth (sun and moon) are 'strangers' to the zodiac, counted among them only for governance, precisely mirrors Swedenborg's teaching that the Lord is in the world but not of it; (7) The number 1468 (years of the great fire) resists simple correspondential reading and may be a later editorial insertion rather than original teaching.
